events.text: A runner brings you a letter folded into a paper crane: {d3_hero}, whom the road-singers of {pw_kingdom} call a hero, asks to cross blades with you at the old ford, before witnesses, at first light. "Not to the death," the letter says. "To the truth."

choices.text: Go to the ford at first light

ok.log: The witnesses go home with a new story, and in it your name comes after the word "beat".

fail.log: It is a good fight, and {d3_hero} wins it. They help you up, which is somehow harder to take than the fall.

choices.text: Send the crane back folded the other way

effects.log: Folded the other way, a paper crane means "not this year". {d3_hero} will understand. The town will talk.

events.text: {d3_hero} is waiting for you in the market square with a practice blade in each hand and half of {pw_kingdom} pretending to buy vegetables nearby. "They say we are the two best in the river towns," {d3_hero} says. "Only one of us can be."

choices.text: Take the practice blade

ok.log: The vegetables are forgotten. When it is over, {d3_hero} laughs and bows, and the square cheers both of you.

fail.log: {d3_hero} disarms you on the ninth exchange. The square cheers anyway. You are not sure it is for you.

choices.text: Say there is no need for only one

effects.log: {d3_hero} looks at you a long moment, then tosses you a pear instead of a blade. It is a good pear.

events.text: The priests of a temple of {pw_world} ask you to fight {d3_hero} at their festival, on the stone floor before the maker's lamp. "The people should see what the world can raise," the old priest says. "The maker should see it too."

choices.text: Fight before the lamp

ok.log: The lamp gutters once, at the end, as if someone very far away had leaned in to watch. The priests say it was the wind.

fail.log: You lose before the lamp, and the priests say the maker loves a good loser too. You are not sure that is in the scriptures.

choices.text: Offer to light the lamp instead

effects.log: You light the lamp. {d3_hero} fights a priest with a broom, and wins, and everyone is happy.

events.text: An old school of {pw_kingdom} is selling its library to pay for a roof. Most of it is almanacs and bad poetry. One box, at the back, is full of breathing charts drawn in a hand older than the kingdom, and nobody has noticed.
events.arc: The Old Books of the World

choices.text: Buy the box and study it

effects.log: Most of it is worn past reading. One sheet is not, and it fits something you already know.

choices.text: Tell the master what is in the box

effects.log: The master goes white, then red, and keeps the box. The roof will be paid for some other way. They will remember who told them.

variants: A school of {pw_kingdom} older than its own walls is selling its books to mend the roof. Almanacs, mostly, and poems nobody should have written. In one forgotten box: breathing charts, in a hand older than the kingdom.

The old school of {pw_kingdom} has a sale of books in its yard. Among the almanacs is a box nobody has opened in a century, full of breathing charts drawn by someone who knew exactly what they were doing.

events.text: Under a burnt inn by the river is a door the Shadow Lodges forgot to brick up: one of their vaults, cleared out in a hurry. On the floor, among broken locks, are torn pages of a method somebody wanted badly enough to steal.
events.arc: The Old Books of the World

choices.text: Go down and gather the pages

effects.log: You gather what the Lodges left. It is more than they meant to leave.

choices.text: Leave the door for the Wardens

effects.log: You tell the Wardens of the roads. They thank you, and what is down there is theirs now.

variants: A burnt inn by the river hides a door the Shadow Lodges never sealed: one of their old vaults, left in a hurry. Among the broken locks lie torn pages of a method someone wanted badly enough to steal.
Under the ashes of a riverside inn, a trapdoor. Below it, a vault the Shadow Lodges emptied in a panic, and on its floor the scattered pages of a stolen method.

events.text: A priest of the maker's temple takes you down to the sutra cellar, where the first people of {pw_world} wrote what they learned about breath and qi on clay. "Nobody can read the old script any more," the priest says. "Perhaps you can."
events.arc: The Old Books of the World

choices.text: Spend the season reading the clay

effects.log: It takes the whole season. At the end you can read a little of it, and the little is worth a great deal.

choices.text: Help the priest copy the clay onto paper

effects.log: You copy what you can. The temple will keep the copies long after the clay crumbles.

variants: In the cellar of the maker's temple, the first people of {pw_world} wrote on clay what they learned of breath and qi. "No one reads the old script now," says the priest with the lamp. "Perhaps you will."

A priest leads you down under the maker's temple, to shelves of clay tablets from the first days of {pw_world}. Breath, qi, the order of the channels, all in a script nobody alive can read. Nearly nobody.

events.text: The elders of your house come to you together, which they never do. "The world is not finished," the eldest says. "The priests say its maker still has to tend it, Dao by Dao. We would like the house to keep a shrine to the maker in the hall. If you allow it."

choices.text: Let the house keep the shrine

effects.log: A small shrine goes up beside the house register. The elders take turns sweeping it. Somewhere, a world is a little better tended.

choices.text: Say the house prays to nobody

effects.log: The elders bow and say nothing. The eldest keeps a candle in her own room anyway.

events.text: Your Second Elder has been going to the river temple every morning before the drills. When you ask, the old fighter scratches their neck. "The priests say the world was made unfinished," they say. "Seemed only right that somebody should help."

choices.text: Go with them tomorrow

effects.log: You go. The temple is small and cold, and the priest is very glad of the company. So, you find, are you.

choices.text: Tell them the drills come first

effects.log: The Second Elder goes before dawn instead. You hear them leave every morning.

events.text: After the exchange match the young of both houses sit on the same benches and eat the same noodles, because that is the custom of {pw_kingdom}. Yours are louder. The others are pretending not to mind.

choices.text: Let them be loud tonight

effects.log: They are loud until the moon is down. The losing side joins in by the end, which is the point of the custom.

choices.text: Remind them how a winner behaves

effects.log: Your young go quiet and pour the other side's tea. The other house's master notices, and nods to you.

events.text: Your youngest champion won the last bout of the match against someone twice their size, and has not stopped grinning since. Half the river towns already know the name.

choices.text: Give them the afternoon off

effects.log: They spend it telling the story. It gets better every time.

choices.text: Make them run the walls anyway

effects.log: They run the walls, still grinning. You find you are grinning too.

events.text: Your young come home from the exchange match with their heads down and their sashes untied. Nobody says anything at supper. The rice goes cold.

choices.text: Tell them what you lost at their age

effects.log: You tell them about the worst match of your life. By the end of it two of them are laughing, and one is taking notes.

choices.text: Double the drills

effects.log: The drills are doubled. Nobody complains. Next time will be different, or they will know why.

events.text: The master of the house that beat yours comes by with a jar of pickled plums. "Your third was good," they say. "Better than ours. Ours was luckier."

choices.text: Accept the plums and the kindness

effects.log: The plums are very sour. The kindness is not. You will remember it at the next match.

choices.text: Ask what your third did wrong

effects.log: The master tells you exactly, at length, with diagrams drawn in plum juice. It is very useful.

events.text: A letter sealed in blue wax: the {d3_school} reminds you, very politely, that your house owes it a favour, and asks for it now. A Lodge cell has moved into the street behind their hall. They need silver for the Wardens, or a good blade at night.

choices.text: Send them the silver

effects.log: You send 150 taels in a plain box. The {d3_school} writes back that the debt is paid.

choices.text: Go yourself, at night

effects.log: You go yourself. The street behind their hall is quiet again by the new moon.

choices.text: Refuse the call

effects.log: You send the letter back unopened. The {d3_school} will tell every school in the kingdom what your favours are worth.

events.text: The old master of the {d3_school} comes to your door in person, which is how you know it is serious. "You owe us," they say. "A flood took our granary. Help us, and the debt is gone."

choices.text: Pay for a new granary

effects.log: You pay 150 taels. The master grips your hand a long moment and goes home with the silver.

choices.text: Bring your people to rebuild it

effects.log: You spend a month carrying beams. The granary stands by harvest, and nobody owes anybody.

choices.text: Say the house cannot spare it

effects.log: The master nods slowly and walks home in the rain. People saw.

events.text: The morning after your lantern went down the river, children are waiting at your gate with lanterns of their own, because they have heard that a retired master teaches anyone who asks.

choices.text: Teach them to fold the lanterns properly

effects.log: You spend the morning folding paper. It is the best morning you have had in years.

choices.text: Send them home with sweets

effects.log: They go home with sweets and stories. The stories have you in them, gentler than you remember being.

events.text: An old enemy of yours was among the witnesses when your lantern went down the river. Now they come to your gate empty-handed and stand there. "I came to see if it was true," they say. "It seems it is."

choices.text: Invite them in for tea

effects.log: You drink tea with someone who once tried to kill you. Neither of you mentions it. It is a strange, quiet afternoon.

choices.text: Nod, and close the gate gently

effects.log: They nod back and leave. It is the last you see of them. That is what the rite is for.

events.text: The kings' envoys bring you the Warden of Wardens' staff at the crossing where three roads meet, where you first swore yourself to the League. The road-wardens of every kingdom are lined up along the verges, and some of them are crying.

choices.text: Take the staff and swear the old oath again

effects.log: You swear it again, louder this time. The roads of the world are yours to keep now.

choices.text: Hand the staff to the oldest warden for a moment first

effects.log: The old warden holds it and weeps openly. Then gives it back. Nobody there will forget it.

events.text: The kingdoms have chosen you Warden of Wardens. That night a Lodge runner leaves a single grey feather on your doorstep. Everyone on the roads knows what a grey feather means: the Lodges think they own you now.

choices.text: Burn the feather in the street

effects.log: You burn it where the runners can see. The Lodges will have to find out the hard way.

choices.text: Keep it, and say nothing

effects.log: You keep it. A Warden of Wardens should know who thinks they own them.

events.text: The kingdoms gave the Warden of Wardens' seat to another captain. At the crossing of three roads the new Warden shakes your hand in front of everyone. "Six years," they say quietly. "Then try me again."

choices.text: Promise them you will

effects.log: They grin. The road-wardens cheer you both, which is the right way to lose.

choices.text: Go home and study who voted how

effects.log: You learn exactly which kings were bought, and by whom. Six years is a long time.

events.text: The Lodges' ledger has gone round every court: your name, the price of the vote, the cup it was left under. The road-wardens you led will not meet your eye. The staff is gone from your hall by morning.

choices.text: Face the kings and admit it

effects.log: You stand before the kings and say it plainly. They do not forgive you, but some of them respect it.

choices.text: Hunt the Lodge elder who sold it

effects.log: You never find the elder. You find three of the runners, and they find out what you are.

events.text: Your champions come back from the ferry landing with their hands bandaged and their faces lit. In the market the stallholders are paying nobody this week, and somebody has painted your house's crest on the Lodges' old toll gate.

choices.text: Go and thank every champion by name

effects.log: You thank each of them. One of them cries, which they will deny for the rest of their life.

choices.text: Plan the next meeting already

effects.log: You sit up with the map until dawn. The Lodges will not be so easy twice.

events.text: The Lodges send your champions home from the ferry landing on a barge, bandaged and fed, with a note pinned to the first one: "Well fought. Try again in two years." It is the politeness that hurts.

choices.text: Keep the note

effects.log: You pin it above your door. Everyone who comes in reads it. That is the point.

choices.text: Burn the note

effects.log: You burn it. Your champions watch it burn and go back to the drills without being asked.

events.text: {d3_holder}, who has stood among the Three Pillars of {pw_world} longer than most people in it have been alive, takes your challenge on a bare hill above {pw_kingdom}. Half the world seems to have walked up the hill to watch.

choices.text: Fight for the seat

ok.log: At the end {d3_holder} sets down their blade and bows to you before the whole hill. The world has a new pillar.

fail.log: {d3_holder} wins, cleanly. "Come back in ten years," they say. "I hope you do." The hill goes home talking about both of you.

choices.text: Ask them to teach you instead

effects.log: {d3_holder} laughs for a long time and then does, for an afternoon. It is worth more than a seat.

events.text: The challenge is set for the old stone bridge over the great river, where the first pillars of {pw_world} were chosen, the priests say. {d3_holder} is already there when you arrive, looking at the water.

choices.text: Step onto the bridge

ok.log: Neither of you falls into the river, which the crowd had been hoping for. But at the end only one of you is standing, and it is you.

fail.log: You lose on the bridge, and {d3_holder} catches your arm before you go over the rail. You will owe them that for a long time.

choices.text: Withdraw the challenge on the bridge

effects.log: You bow and withdraw. {d3_holder} bows back. The crowd is very disappointed. The river does not care.

events.text: {d3_holder} is old now, and everybody knows it. Their students stand behind them at the meeting place with very hard faces. "Do not go easy on me," {d3_holder} says. "I will know."

choices.text: Fight with everything you have

ok.log: You give them everything, and it is just enough. {d3_holder} smiles as if this was what they had wanted all along.

fail.log: Old or not, {d3_holder} is still a pillar of the world. You learn that the hard way, in front of their students.

choices.text: Ask them to name their own successor instead

effects.log: {d3_holder} looks at their students for a long time and says they will think about it. It is the kindest thing you have done all year.

events.text: A young fighter from the far side of {pw_world}, {d3_holder}, walks into the town with a letter for you and the whole road following: a challenge for your seat among the Three Pillars.

choices.text: Meet them, as a pillar must

ok.log: You keep your seat. {d3_holder} takes the loss well, and asks if they can stay and learn. Perhaps.

fail.log: {d3_holder} is better than anyone thought. The seat is theirs now. You bow, because a pillar of the world bows.

choices.text: Give up the seat without a fight

effects.log: You give the seat to {d3_holder} with your own hands. The world thinks less of you, or more. It cannot decide.

events.text: {d3_holder} has been beating every master in {pw_kingdom} one by one, and now the road leads to your door. "I do not want your seat," they say. "I want to know if I could take it."

choices.text: Show them

ok.log: They could not. They leave with a bow and the best lesson of their life.

fail.log: They could. The seat is theirs, though they look almost sorry about it.

choices.text: Tell them to come back in ten years

effects.log: {d3_holder} goes away to train. In ten years they will come back. You know it.

events.text: {d3_foe}, who has bought half the river trade of {pw_kingdom} in three years, sends a polite letter asking to buy {d3_hold}. The price is insulting. The letter says, in the last line, that they always get what they ask for.

choices.text: Go and explain to {d3_foe} in person

ok.log: You explain. {d3_foe} understands, in the end, after the third exchange. They will not ask again.

fail.log: Their guards are better than you expected, and {d3_foe} gets a piece of what you hold after all.

choices.text: Pay them to go away for a year

effects.log: You pay them a year of what it earns. {d3_foe} goes away, smiling, for a year.

choices.text: Let them have part of it

effects.log: You let them have part of it. It will cost less than a war, this year.

events.text: Men with clubs appear at {d3_hold} one morning, sent by {d3_foe}, who says the land was promised to their grandmother by a king nobody remembers. The keepers send for you.

choices.text: Go and meet the clubs yourself

ok.log: The clubs go home. So does {d3_foe}'s grandmother's promise.

fail.log: There are more clubs than you were told. {d3_foe} keeps what they took.

choices.text: Pay {d3_foe} to forget the grandmother

effects.log: You pay a year of what it earns. The grandmother is forgotten, for now.

choices.text: Let the land go

effects.log: You let part of it go. The keepers look at you as if you were someone else.

events.text: {d3_foe} has been to every priest and every judge in {pw_kingdom}, and now has a scroll with three seals saying that {d3_hold} is theirs. The scroll is a lie. The seals are real.

choices.text: Take the scroll from them

ok.log: You take the scroll and burn it in front of the judges. Nobody brings it up again.

fail.log: {d3_foe} keeps the scroll and a piece of your holding with it.

choices.text: Pay the judges more than they did

effects.log: You pay a year of what it earns, to the right people. The scroll is found to be a forgery.

choices.text: Let the scroll stand

effects.log: You let it stand. Some fights are not worth the price.

events.text: A third of the great temple to the maker is standing: the foundation, the steps and one wall with its carvings. A storm in the night knocks down the scaffolding. The masons stand in the mud waiting to hear what you will do.

choices.text: Rebuild it stronger, at your own cost

effects.log: You pay for oak instead of pine. The temple will stand longer than any of you.

choices.text: Tell them to carry on as they can

effects.log: They carry on. The temple will be finished. It will not be quite what you hoped.

events.text: The great temple is two thirds built when the priests of an older shrine come to say it will take their people away. They are not wrong. They are also very afraid.

choices.text: Give the old shrine a hall in the new temple

effects.log: The old priests weep, and bring their oldest lamp to the new hall. The temple is better for it.

choices.text: Tell them the maker needs one temple, not two

effects.log: The old priests go away. The temple is finished on time. Something is missing from it, and you know what.

events.text: A third of the Long Road between the kingdoms is paved. A lord of {pw_kingdom} has started charging a toll on your part of it, and the merchants are going round by the old mud tracks.

choices.text: Pay off the lord

effects.log: You pay the lord to stop. The merchants come back to the road.

choices.text: Build round the lord's land

effects.log: You build round. It takes five years more, and the road bends where it should not.

events.text: The Long Road reaches the mountains, and the mountain folk do not want it. "Roads bring soldiers," their headwoman says. "Soldiers bring kings."

choices.text: Let the mountain folk choose the way

effects.log: The road goes where they say. It is longer, and it is loved.

choices.text: Go straight through

effects.log: The road goes straight through. The mountain folk watch it pass, and do not use it.

events.text: The bronze for the Ward-Bell is half poured when the founders find a crack in the mould. Pour now, and the bell may sing false. Break the mould, and the work goes back years.

choices.text: Break the mould and start again

effects.log: You break it. The new mould is perfect. The bell will sing true, later.

choices.text: Have them patch the crack with clay and prayer

effects.log: They patch it, and pray. Somehow it holds, and the bronze runs clean.

events.text: The Ward-Bell hangs in its frame, waiting for its voice. The old founder says a bell's first note must be struck by someone the world trusts, or it will never be believed.

choices.text: Strike it yourself

effects.log: You strike it. The note goes out over the whole of {pw_world}, and every dog in it howls at once.

choices.text: Let a child of the town strike it

effects.log: A child strikes it, very hard, and laughs. The bell will be believed.

events.text: The keepers of your lands send word: {d3_beast} has been seen at the edge of the hills, closer than any year before. The farmers are bringing their animals into the town.

choices.text: Go out and meet it at the hills

ok.log: You turn {d3_beast} back at the hills. The farmers take their animals home.

fail.log: {d3_beast} goes past you and through the fields. You are carried home, and your lands pay for it.

choices.text: Leave it to the keepers and the walls

effects.log: The keepers hold the walls. The fields outside them are lost for the season.

choices.text: Let it pass and rebuild after

effects.log: It passes. You rebuild after. It costs more than you would like.

events.text: Every well on your lands has gone bitter overnight. The old people say {d3_beast} has woken in the deep water, and that it wakes like this only when something it wants is close.

choices.text: Go down to the deep water

ok.log: You go down. When you come up the wells are sweet again, and you do not talk about what you saw.

fail.log: You come up alone and hurt, and the wells stay bitter for a year.

choices.text: Have the wells dug deeper

effects.log: The new wells cost a great deal and are sweet. The old ones stay bitter.

events.text: THE GREAT CALAMITY. The sky over your lands is the colour of an old bruise, and {d3_beast} is coming down out of the hills with the whole weight of the world's anger behind it. The priests say it comes once in a hundred years. They have never seen it.

choices.text: Stand in its road

ok.log: You stand in its road, and it stops. The priests will write this down for a hundred years.

fail.log: It goes through you and through your lands. You live. Not everything you held does.

choices.text: Get the people out, and let the land go

effects.log: Everyone lives. The land does not, this time.

events.text: THE GREAT CALAMITY. The river has risen higher than any mark on any bridge in {pw_world}, and in the brown water something long and very old is swimming towards your lands. People are climbing onto their roofs.

choices.text: Go out on the water to meet it

ok.log: The water goes down with it. When the roofs are empty again, people come to touch your sleeve.

fail.log: The water and the beast take what they want. You are pulled out of the river by a ferry child.

choices.text: Take boats to the roofs

effects.log: You spend three days in a boat. Nobody drowns. The lands are another matter.

events.text: The beasts of {pw_world} are moving. Not one but hundreds, out of the hills behind {d3_beast}, in a tide that has not come in living memory. The Wardens are raising a line across the valley road, and they are short of people.

choices.text: Take a place in the line

ok.log: The line holds. When the tide turns back into the hills, the Wardens give you a place at their fire for life.

fail.log: The line bends and you are carried back with it, hurt. It holds, in the end, without you.

choices.text: Lead the townspeople out by the back roads

effects.log: You lead them out. Nobody is lost. The Wardens hold, barely.

choices.text: Stand aside

effects.log: You stand aside. The tide passes. People remember who stood where.

events.text: From the town walls you can see them coming: the beasts of {pw_world}, a dark line across the barley, with {d3_beast} at the head. Behind you a thousand people are waiting to see what the strongest person in town will do.

choices.text: Go out over the wall

ok.log: You go over the wall, and the dark line breaks around you like water round a stone.

fail.log: You go over the wall and come back over it, hurt, with the line still coming. The walls hold, just.

choices.text: Organise the walls

effects.log: You put every bow in town where it does most good. The tide breaks on the walls.

choices.text: Buy what the beasts leave behind

effects.log: After the tide, hides and horns are cheap. You buy them all.

events.text: You stand as high as the heaven of {pw_world} lets a mortal stand, and the heaven has noticed. A lesser god of {pw_heaven} comes down in a column of light into your courtyard and asks, very politely, what you think you are doing.

choices.text: Say you are going higher, and show it

roll.foeName: a lesser god of the world

ok.log: The god looks at you for a long time, then goes back up the column of light. The sky feels a little higher afterwards.

fail.log: The god does not fight you. It only lets you feel, for one breath, how far up the sky goes. You sit down very suddenly.

choices.text: Bow, and say you only want to protect the people

effects.log: The god bows back. "Then protect them," it says, and goes. The courtyard smells of incense for a week.

choices.text: Go quiet, and let the sky forget you

effects.log: You live quietly for a year. The sky forgets you. Mostly.

events.text: Lightning out of a clear sky, three times, on the same spot of your roof. The priests come running. "The heaven of {pw_world} does not want anyone standing so close to it," they say. "It never has."

choices.text: Climb onto the roof and wait for the fourth

ok.log: The fourth bolt does not come. Whatever was asking has its answer.

fail.log: The fourth bolt comes. You live, and your hair stands up for a month.

choices.text: Have the priests pray for you

effects.log: The priests pray all night. The sky stays clear. You are not sure which of you it was listening to.

events.text: {d3_beast}, which the maker of {pw_world} set to walk its hills before there were people in it, comes down to the edge of your town at dusk and looks at you. Only at you. The dogs do not bark.

choices.text: Go out to it, alone

effects.log: You go out. It lowers its great head, and you put your hand on it. Something passes between you that has no words.

choices.text: Bow from the gate

effects.log: You bow. It looks at you a little longer, and goes back into the hills.

events.text: Your eyes see what other people do not, and tonight they see {d3_beast} standing in the river shallows, as old as the world, watching you back. It has never let anyone see it before.

choices.text: Walk into the river to it

effects.log: The water is cold. It waits. When you reach it, it lets you stand beside it until morning.

choices.text: Tell the priests what you saw

effects.log: The priests write it down. They have waited a long time for someone to see it.

events.text: A beast you keep starts acting strangely: it stops eating, watches the hills, and at night it answers something that calls from very far away. The old people say {d3_beast} is calling the beasts of {pw_world} to it.

choices.text: Follow your beast to the hills

effects.log: You follow it all night. At dawn, on a bare hill, {d3_beast} is waiting, and lets you come close.

choices.text: Keep your beast home

effects.log: You keep it home. It forgives you after a month. You hope.

events.text: You send word to {npc}: a duel, at the ferry landing of {pw_kingdom}, at dawn, before witnesses. {He} sends the ferry-boy back with one word. Yes.

choices.text: Meet {him} at dawn

ok.log: Before the first ferry crosses, {npc} is on one knee on the landing, and the ferry-folk are very quiet.

fail.log: {npc} is better than you hoped. The ferry-folk will tell it up and down the river for a month.

choices.text: Send the ferry-boy back with an apology

effects.log: You withdraw the challenge. The ferry-boy tells everyone on the way back.

events.text: Your challenge to {npc} is read aloud in the temple square of {pw_world}, as the custom is. By evening every stall has an opinion on who will win, and the priests have set out benches.

choices.text: Fight before the temple

ok.log: The benches are full when {npc} goes down. The priests say the maker was watching. The stallholders say they knew all along.

fail.log: {npc} wins before the temple, and the benches cheer. You are carried home by people you do not know.

choices.text: Call it off at the last moment

effects.log: You call it off. The benches are taken away. Some of the stallholders lose more than face.

events.text: You send {npc} a challenge with no limits written on it: a duel to the death. Witnesses gather at the old shrine to the maker on the hill above {pw_kingdom}. Only one of you is meant to walk down.

choices.text: Fight to the death

ok.log: It is long and silent. At the end {npc} is on the ground and cannot rise, and everyone on the hill waits to see what you will do.

fail.log: It goes the wrong way from the first exchange.
fail.deathCause: a duel to the death with {npc}

choices.text: Call it off before the first exchange

effects.log: You lower your weapon. {npc} looks at you a long time, and goes down the hill. The witnesses do not.

events.text: {npc} accepts your challenge to the death with a letter in a fine hand, and adds at the bottom that {he} has asked the priests of the river temple to burn a lamp for whichever of you does not come back.

choices.text: Go to the river temple

ok.log: When it is over {npc} is on the temple steps, beaten, and the lamp is still burning. It is up to you whose it is.

fail.log: {npc} was right to ask for the lamp.
fail.deathCause: a duel to the death with {npc}

choices.text: Send the priests word that nobody needs the lamp

effects.log: You withdraw. The priests put the lamp out. {npc} sends no answer at all.

events.text: A road-singer at the ford of {pw_kingdom} is singing about you, getting most of it wrong, and at the end of every verse gives you a name. The ferry-folk are already singing it back.

choices.text: Answer to it

effects.log: You do not correct the singer. By the next ford, it is your name.

choices.text: Keep what you are called

effects.log: You tell the singer your own name, kindly. The singer looks disappointed and sings the verse again anyway.

events.text: The priests of a temple of {pw_world} have written a new name beside yours in the book of the people who did great things for the world. They ask you, very carefully, if it is all right.

choices.text: Answer to it

effects.log: You say yes. The ink is dry by evening.

choices.text: Keep what you are called

effects.log: You ask them to cross it out. They do, so gently that you can still read it.

events.text: The people of {pw_world} do not wait for anyone to tell them what you are. In every kingdom a shrine goes up with your face painted badly on it, and on the first morning there are flowers in front of every one.

choices.text: Visit the first shrine in plain clothes

effects.log: Nobody recognises you. An old woman tells you all about yourself. Most of it is kind, and none of it is true.

choices.text: Ask the priests to keep the maker's lamp first

effects.log: The priests put the maker's lamp above your picture. The people do not mind. The world is better tended for it.

events.text: In {pw_world} they say your name only in whispers now, and they leave bowls of rice at crossroads so you will pass by. Nobody asked them to. Fear that old makes its own rites.

choices.text: Leave the rice where it lies

effects.log: The rice is left. The crossroads stay quiet. That is all they wanted.

choices.text: Eat from one bowl, so they know you saw

effects.log: You eat from one bowl. By morning the story has reached every kingdom.

events.text: On the far shore of {pw_world} something is waiting that was one of the first people once, before there were kingdoms. It has cultivated in the dark since the world was young, and it remembers the maker's voice. It does not remember kindness.

choices.text: Face it, and lay it to rest

effects.log: You meet it soul to soul, and tell it the world went on without it.

choices.text: Face it, and devour it

effects.log: You meet it soul to soul, and you are hungrier than it is.

choices.text: Burn offerings at the temple, and send it elsewhere

effects.log: You go back and burn what you can spare at the maker's lamp.

choices.text: Flee back into your body

effects.log: You run for the lamp in the window.

events.text: The dead of the Lodge War walk the far shore of {pw_world} in a line, still carrying the ledgers they died for. One of them steps out of the line towards you, and its ledger has your name in it.

choices.text: Face it, and lay it to rest

effects.log: You take the ledger from its hands and close it.

choices.text: Face it, and devour it

effects.log: You take the ledger, and then you take the rest of it.

choices.text: Pay its debt in offerings

effects.log: You promise offerings at the river temple. The line moves on.

choices.text: Flee back into your body

effects.log: You run for the lamp in the window, and the line does not follow.

events.text: Your kingdom is a week old. Its court is five people in a borrowed hall. The first petition is a farmer asking for a bridge, the second a captain asking for pay, and the third a scholar from {pw_kingdom} offering to write the laws.

choices.text: Build the bridge first

effects.log: The bridge goes up by harvest. The farmers remember who built it.

choices.text: Pay the soldiers first

effects.log: The soldiers cheer you at the next muster. The farmers wait, and notice.

choices.text: Let the scholar write the laws

effects.log: The laws are long and fair and nobody reads them. They hold anyway.

events.text: An envoy of {pw_kingdom}, the oldest kingdom of {pw_world}, rides in with a scroll: your kingdom may stand, if it sends tribute every spring and its ruler kneels once a year.

choices.text: Kneel and pay

effects.log: You kneel. The envoy smiles. Your court watches, and some of them remember.

choices.text: Send the envoy home with a gift and no answer

effects.log: The envoy goes. The answer that is not an answer travels ahead.

choices.text: Tear up the scroll in front of the court

effects.log: Your court roars. Somewhere to the east, an army begins to gather.

events.text: An army of {pw_kingdom} is camped across the river from your border, and its general has sent a polite note asking you to surrender two valleys or come and take them back yourself.

choices.text: Ride out at the head of your army

roll.foeName: the general of the old kingdom

ok.log: You ride at the front. Their line breaks at the river. Your kingdom is larger by a valley.

fail.log: The line breaks. You are carried off the field. Your kingdom loses two towns before the peace.

choices.text: Buy a peace

effects.log: The army turns round. Your treasury is lighter and your borders the same.

choices.text: Give them one valley and keep the other

effects.log: They take the valley. Your people in it cross the river to you with everything they can carry.

events.text: The rice failed in the low fields of your kingdom, and families are walking north on the roads with their children on their backs. Your granaries are full. The army's are fuller.

choices.text: Open the granaries

effects.log: Nobody starves. The families walk back south in spring, and they talk about you on the way.

choices.text: Keep the grain for the army

effects.log: The army eats. The villages do not forget.

events.text: Your court has split in two: the captains who want more soldiers, and the scholars who want more schools. Each side brings you a list of the other side's names.

choices.text: Side with the captains

effects.log: Three scholars are sent home. The ledgers get worse within a year.

choices.text: Side with the scholars

effects.log: The captains grumble over their tea. The ledgers balance for the first time.

choices.text: Burn both lists unread

effects.log: Both camps are furious with you, which is the same as being at peace.

events.text: A recruiter from a famous school of {pw_kingdom}, passing through, laughs at your forms in the village square and says no farmer's child will ever amount to anything. {npc} walks over. The recruiter stops laughing, and then cannot quite remember why.
events.arc: A Parent Who Hides Their Peak

choices.text: Say nothing: you will handle it yourself

effects.log: {npc} only asks the recruiter for directions, and the moment passes. You practise twice as hard that winter, out of spite.

choices.text: Ask {npc} what was said to the recruiter

effects.log: {npc} says it was the weather. The recruiter left town before dawn, and the story is everywhere.

events.text: {npc} closes the door, sits you down and stops pretending. The pressure of {his} qi fills the room like deep water. "I stood among the best of {pw_world} once," {he} says. "I came home to be quiet. But you are going out into it whether I like it or not."
events.arc: A Parent Who Hides Their Peak

choices.text: Ask {npc} to teach you

effects.log: The lessons start before dawn the next day and do not stop.

choices.text: Ask why {he} hid it

effects.log: It is a long story, with a war, a ferry and a grave in it. You understand {npc} better at the end of it.
